title: Possession (1981)… what on Earth did I just watch?

commenti.body:
The acting is very much intentional, its 20th century  Polish expressionism. In fact the director expressed frustration at first because he had a hard time getting Sam Neill and Adjani to commit to the role. They wanted to act more traditionally out of fear of looking like fools.

Polish expressionism is about acting like youre on a stage, talking loud, using the whole stage, using your whole body to express emotions.

Its fine if you dont like that style, or went into the film with the wrong mindset... like believing it to be a more traditionally horror movie and not an experimental movie about divorce and the corruption of communism... but to call it Tommy Wiseau-esque is just wrong.

Wiseau set out to create an oscar winning drama and failed. Zulawski created the film just how he wanted it. Everything in it is intentional, and if thats not your thing, thats okay.

Maybe it just isn't for you. For me, the joy of watching *Possession* lies in its ecstatic freedom. The camera, performances, and tone all feel deliriously untethered to convention or tastefulness. The film is truly *wild* in its expressive and grotesque depiction of infidelity.

To grab at a low hanging example of something similar, I think Nicolas Cage approaches acting very intentionally with a similar concept in mind. Sometimes it works in a movie, and sometimes it doesn’t, but I have seen audiences really struggle to understand what he is even attempting to do.

It is singularly grotesque, ugly, unhinged, and hysterical. It DOES make me unapologetically laugh, but there's a queasy, uncomfortable sense of dread and suspense that runs right along side it. It's one of my all-time top 10, because it makes me feel a very specific type of horrified/thrilled/repulsed/giddy that nothing else on Earth does.

As an expression of the absolute psychosis you go through during a traumatic relationship death goes, God only made one of these movies.

Yes the style is intentional.

Also -- it's West Berlin before the Wall came down. This was a *very* wild place -- characters like the wife's lover really existed. Believe me, I was there.
